assumptions.assumption: The engine CLI (claude) actually emits a durable, per-session usage record (the session JSONL sidecar) for INTERACTIVE bare-PTY sessions — not just for stream-json one-shot jobs — and that record contains real token/time/cost fields rather than only conversation turns.
assumptions.basis: The whole capture seam is premised on 'the engine's own sidecar'. One-shot jobs report usage in result envelopes, but an interactive ConPTY session is a raw TUI; if the interactive sidecar omits usage or only some models/versions write it, criterion (1) has no data source and the plan silently degrades to 'unmeasured' everywhere — which satisfies the honesty contract but fails the North Star's actual point (measured truth).

assumptions.assumption: A PTY session's sidecar file can be UNAMBIGUOUSLY correlated to its Anchor session_id — e.g. via the worktree cwd → ~/.claude/projects/<slug> mapping plus mtime/window — even with many concurrent sessions, engine switches mid-session (claude↔gemini), and sessions that share a project path.
assumptions.basis: Two steps downstream: the rollup dedup key is session_id, so a wrong sidecar match doesn't just miss cost, it ATTRIBUTES another session's cost — a fabrication, violating criterion (2). Anchor sessions run in per-session worktrees (helpful) but v7 'general' sessions and switch_engine relaunches in the SAME worktree stress the mapping; the plan assumes a deterministic join exists.

assumptions.assumption: The sidecar survives every end path long enough to be finalized — including kill (worktree reaped), reconcile-dead after a server crash, the NSSM warm-drain park, and boot-time reaping — i.e. usage lives OUTSIDE the worktree and finalize-on-reconcile can run arbitrarily late against a file that still exists.
assumptions.basis: Criterion (1) demands finalization on finish/kill/close/reconcile-dead. Kill reaps the worktree and reconcile-dead by definition runs after the process died (possibly after a reboot). If the usage record lives in or is cleaned with the worktree, or the engine prunes old session files, the most common real-world end paths (crash, restart) are exactly the ones that lose the cost record.

assumptions.assumption: Dollar cost is derivable from engine-REPORTED data alone (a costUSD-like field), so Anchor never needs its own model-pricing table; and on a subscription (Max) host that engine-reported $ is still meaningful enough to display as 'measured truth'.
assumptions.basis: Criterion (2) forbids estimation/interpolation. If the sidecar reports tokens but not $, computing $ requires a pricing table Anchor maintains — which drifts with model releases and IS an estimate. And on subscription auth the marginal $ is notional; the North Star's '$' column may need to be honestly reframed (tokens/time measured, $ derived-or-absent) — an unstated product decision the plan rests on.

assumptions.assumption: The pinned sidecar fixture stays representative of the real engine's format across CLI upgrades — the format is stable, or a drift-detection tripwire (live smoke in criterion 1/7) will actually fire before months of silent zero-capture.
assumptions.basis: This is exactly the v11 lesson and the summarizer stream-json bug replayed: stubs stayed green while prod parsed nothing. The STUB GATE proves the parser matches the FIXTURE, not the engine; the plan assumes the one live smoke run plus healthcheck walk is enough to catch format drift, but the healthcheck walk is itself stubbed (criterion 6), so post-deploy drift has no scheduled detector.

assumptions.assumption: A read-only 'orientation' prompt can be auto-executed SAFELY — i.e. a seeded engine turn that 'loads docs and narrates' can be mechanically guaranteed not to take mutating actions, and the read-only/ACTION classification of any given resume prompt is decidable in code, not by judgment.
assumptions.basis: Criterion (5) resolves the v10 paste-NOT-submit fork by auto-submitting one class of prompt. But the engine executing an auto-submitted prompt has its full tool belt in a real worktree; 'read-only' is a property of the PROMPT TEXT, not an enforced sandbox (permission_mode='plan' exists for jobs but the assumption is it can be applied to the interactive resume turn too). If a narration turn can ever edit files, the locked no-auto-submit safety contract is breached, not just a test.

assumptions.assumption: Auto-executing an orientation turn on EVERY tile click is acceptable in cost and side effects: each click spends real tokens (which the new capture will now visibly meter), spawns a real PTY+worktree, and the user won't experience this as 'clicking around my dashboard costs money and litters live sessions'.
assumptions.basis: Second-order effect of (5)+(1) combined: the feature that makes cost visible also adds a new cost source on the most casual UI gesture. The plan assumes browse-clicks are rare enough, or that orientation turns are cheap enough, that the rollup isn't dominated by the instrumentation itself; otherwise the fix creates the next honesty complaint.

assumptions.assumption: session_id-keyed dedup is sufficient to prevent double-counting across ALL provenance combinations that actually occur: persisted docs (discovered) + new RUN cost record, legacy (store_lane, job_id) job dedup, grass dev-sessions, engine-switch relaunches, and continue/resume sessions seeded from a prior one.
assumptions.basis: Criterion (3) tests exactly one pair (docs+cost same session). Two steps downstream, the messy cases are: a resume session narrating an old session (two session_ids, one logical effort), switch_engine (one session_id, two engine sidecars), and v12 single-session efforts vs legacy 3-chain efforts rendered uniformly. The plan assumes the existing effort/rollup identity model has one stable join key; the codebase history (dedup by (store_lane, job_id), lane-qualified build:: ids) shows identity has been the recurring soft spot.

assumptions.assumption: The diag-B2 tile failures (blank window, context-free blue restart) are DETERMINISTIC functions of captured registry state — reproducible from fixtures without a live PTY, timing, or WebSocket race in the loop.
assumptions.basis: Criterion (4) mandates reproduce-first from registry-state fixtures. If any of the failures is actually a race (attach-before-replay, fit-before-layout — both have prior history in this codebase, e.g. the W5 re-fit fix), the fixture repro will pass while the field bug persists, and the 'fixed' screenshot sign-off proves the wrong thing.

assumptions.assumption: Every tile class has enough persisted material for a non-blank, ORIENTING open: cached summaries / persisted docs exist for the sessions users actually click — i.e. summarize-on-finish and doc-persist coverage is already near-universal in real data, so narration has substance and rarely falls to the honest-degraded seed.
assumptions.basis: Criterion (5)'s 'narrates what was done/produced/next' presumes source material. The W3 synthesized-seed work exists precisely because many discovered efforts have NO record and NO cached summary; if that's the common case in John's real projects, resume 'works' but narrates near-nothing, missing the North Star's felt outcome while passing every test.

assumptions.assumption: Gemini-engine sessions either expose an equivalent usage record or the plan explicitly scopes them to the 'unmeasured' state — and the W8 both-subscriptions host means a meaningful fraction of sessions WILL be Gemini, so this is a mainline path, not an edge.
assumptions.basis: The North Star says EVERY session. The capture seam is described in Claude-sidecar terms; agy/Gemini's on-disk usage story is unverified. Without an explicit decision, Gemini sessions become permanent 'unmeasured' rows that read as a broken feature, or worse, someone later 'fixes' them with an estimate — violating criterion (2).

assumptions.assumption: The existing v4 rollup and v8 persist test suites can stay GREEN UNMODIFIED while the rollup's data model grows a new RUN-provenance cost source and a distinct 'unmeasured' state — i.e. the new states are purely additive and no existing assertion pins 'interactive sessions contribute 0'.
assumptions.basis: Criterion (2) pins 'suites stay green unmodified' as the honesty regression guard. But the current suites were written when PTY sessions contributed 0 BY DESIGN; if any test asserts that zero (or asserts rollup totals exactly), the criterion is self-contradictory and the builder will be forced to either modify the suite (breaking the criterion) or contort the design around a stale assertion.

assumptions.assumption: The one-time before/after undercount measurement (criterion 7) is actually computable: historical sessions' sidecars still exist on disk with usage intact for at least one real project, and the 'after' backfill can attribute them to sessions retroactively.
assumptions.basis: Turning derived-I1 into an observed number requires retroactive data. Engine session files may have been pruned, live in per-machine dirs, or predate worktree-cwd conventions; if so the measurement degrades to 'rollup went up by X after deploy' with no ground-truth denominator — still useful, but the criterion as worded assumes recoverable history.

assumptions.assumption: A sidecar-location seam (env-overridable, like ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD/ANCHOR_PTY_BACKEND) can fully isolate tests and the 5AM healthcheck from the REAL ~/.claude session store — no test path ever globs the live sidecar directory.
assumptions.basis: Criterion (6). The real sidecar dir is a global, user-level location shared with every other Claude session on PUTER (including the very session running the tests). Without a hard seam, a healthcheck walk could match the developer's live session files — nondeterministic flakes at best, cross-contaminated cost records at worst; the codebase's every prior subsystem needed exactly such a seam.

assumptions.assumption: Finalize-on-end is idempotent and single-writer under the known-corruptible registry write path — concurrent end paths (user clicks kill while reconcile runs; drain during close) won't write two cost records or tear the effort index.
assumptions.basis: The 2026-07-08 architecture review flagged non-atomic writes in rnd_registry/effort_history as the #1 durability bug, and end-path handlers already race (close vs reconcile vs boot-reaper). The plan assumes the cost-record write can be made upsert-idempotent keyed on session_id atop that substrate; if not, the no-double-counting criterion (3) can fail intermittently in ways the deterministic suite never sees.

assumptions.assumption: 'Warm' resume at click-time is compatible with resource reality: opening a real PTY + worktree per clicked tile (including brownfield/discovered ones) doesn't collide with the orphan-reaper/zombie-hunter heuristics or accumulate parked worktrees past what the boot reaper now preserves.
assumptions.basis: W6 made the reaper KEEP parked-idle worktrees and the zombie-hunter spare live-owner sessions; every-tile-opens-a-session multiplies exactly the population those safety systems reason over. The plan assumes current liveness/ownership rules classify orientation sessions correctly two subsystems away — historically where Anchor's false-kill hazards have lived.

premortem.mode: Interactive sessions still roll up as zero: the bare-PTY sidecar contains conversation turns with per-message usage blocks but no session-level cost/duration record, and on some CLI versions/config (verbose off, resumed sessions) usage fields are absent or reset per resume — the capture parser finds nothing it recognizes as a cost record and honestly emits 'unmeasured' for nearly every interactive session, which is exactly the zero-by-omission the North Star forbids, just relabeled.
premortem.cause: The plan generalized from the stream-json one-shot format (which has an explicit result envelope with cost/duration) to interactive JSONL, which only carries per-message usage that must be summed and can be partial across /resume boundaries.
premortem.mitigation: Before building the pipeline, run a spike that opens a REAL interactive claude PTY, does 3 turns, kills it, and diffs the sidecar against the parser's expectations; design the parser as sum-over-message-usage (not find-the-total-record) with an explicit 'partial: resumed elsewhere' state; gate the whole plan on this spike's findings.

premortem.mode: Cost records attributed to the WRONG session: two concurrent sessions in the same project (a grass dev session and a lane session sharing a worktree base, or a continue-session relaunch) produce multiple JSONL files under the same ~/.claude/projects/<slug>; the mtime-window heuristic picks the wrong one, so one session shows double cost and its sibling shows zero — the rollup is now confidently wrong, which is worse than honestly zero.
premortem.cause: cwd-slug + mtime is a heuristic, not an identity. Engine switches relaunch in the SAME worktree (same slug, new sidecar), the W6 close/reopen path reuses worktrees, and PTY start times cluster within seconds during auto-advance chains.
premortem.mitigation: Stop correlating after the fact: capture the engine session UUID at START time — parse it from the PTY banner/first sidecar line created after launch (watch the slug dir for the new file within a tight window while holding the session lock), store it ON the registry record (engine_session_id), and treat any record without a captured UUID as honestly 'uncorrelated', never best-guess.

premortem.mode: Finalize-on-reconcile runs weeks later against sidecars that no longer exist: the engine CLI's own retention (cleanupPeriodDays-style pruning) or a user 'claude clean' deleted the JSONL, so every session that ended via server-crash/reconcile-dead or long park finalizes to 'unmeasured' — and the backfill criterion (7) is silently uncomputable for the same reason.
premortem.cause: Assumption 3 checked that usage lives outside the worktree but not that the SIDE-CAR store has its own garbage collector with a default retention shorter than 'arbitrarily late'.
premortem.mitigation: Finalize EAGERLY: snapshot the usage summary into .anchor/ at every end path (kill, close, drain-park, even a periodic heartbeat copy for long-running sessions), so reconcile-dead reads Anchor's own snapshot, never the live store; treat the ~/.claude sidecar as a transient source, not the durable record.

premortem.mode: The dashboard displays dollar figures that are fabricated-by-multiplication or blank: on the Max subscription host the interactive sidecar carries no costUSD (or carries $0.00), so the UI either shows $0 'measured truth' for sessions that burned 400k tokens, or someone quietly adds a pricing table — violating the no-own-pricing-table premise — and it drifts stale after the next model launch.
premortem.cause: Engine-reported dollars are an API-metering concept; subscription hosts meter in rate-limit units, not dollars, so 'derivable from engine-reported data alone' was only true for the one-shot API path.
premortem.mitigation: Make TOKENS+TIME the first-class measured truth and dollars an OPTIONAL display shown only when the engine actually reported a nonzero costUSD; render 'N tok · Xm (subscription)' otherwise. Decide this at plan level now so no wave 'helpfully' adds a pricing table.

premortem.mode: Silent zero-capture for months after a CLI upgrade: an engine update renames/nests the usage fields, the pinned fixture keeps every test green, and the live-smoke tripwire never fires because it was implemented inside the 5AM healthcheck where ALL model calls are stubbed by ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD per the existing healthcheck contract — so nothing in production ever compares a REAL sidecar to the parser.
premortem.cause: The project's own (correct) test discipline — never live claude in tests/healthcheck — structurally conflicts with a drift tripwire that only works against the real format, and nobody resolved the contradiction.
premortem.mitigation: Add a cheap NON-model drift check the healthcheck CAN run live: parse the most recent real sidecar already on disk (read-only, no spawn) and warn (report.warn, per the severity rule) when zero of the last N real session files yield usage; additionally stamp each rollup with capture-rate ('measured 3/17 sessions this week') so decay is visible on the dashboard itself, not just in reports.

premortem.mode: An 'orientation' turn mutates the project: the resumed session opens with a trio skill seed (Foreman/Crucible) whose own instructions say to continue the build; the read-only prompt wrapper is advice the model can override, permission plan-mode is either unavailable or unenforced on a bare interactive PTY, and one tile click resumes a half-finished Foreman wave that edits files and commits. The 'decidable in code' read-only classifier turns out to be prompt-text pattern-matching, i.e. judgment with extra steps.
premortem.cause: Read-only-ness of an agentic turn is a property of the harness (permission mode/tool allowlist), not of the prompt, and the interactive ConPTY path has no harness-level enforcement seam today.
premortem.mitigation: Split the feature: tile click opens a WARM but PASSIVE view (cached summary + doc-role narration + the pending NEXT-PROMPT as a paste-not-submit, reusing the v10 mechanism) with zero auto-executed engine turns; any narrating engine turn requires an explicit user Enter. If auto-narration survives, it must run through a harness-enforced read-only mode (e.g. a one-shot plan-mode job, not the live PTY) — never a seeded interactive turn.

premortem.mode: Dashboard browsing becomes expensive and littered: a user reviewing a project clicks 8 tiles, spawning 8 PTYs + 8 worktrees, each auto-spending an orientation turn; the new metering makes the cost visible ('why did looking at my dashboard cost 250k tokens?'), the session bar fills with live sessions nobody asked for, and trust in tiles drops to pre-fix levels for the opposite reason.
premortem.cause: Auto-execute-on-click couples a read gesture (inspect) to a spend+spawn action (resume), and Layout-D makes tiles the primary navigation surface.
premortem.mitigation: Two-step affordance: click = passive warm view (free, no PTY); an explicit '▶ Resume live' control = spawn + orientation. Cap concurrent click-spawned sessions (reuse an already-live session for the same effort instead of spawning a sibling) and auto-park orientation-only sessions after N idle minutes.

premortem.mode: Double-counted efforts inflate the rollup: a session's docs persist to main (v8 keystone) and get re-discovered by brownfield_scan as a discovered effort while the same session's new RUN cost record also counts; engine-switch relaunches produce two sidecars summed twice onto one session; a continue-session pair each ingest the SAME resumed engine conversation (the engine resumes/copies history into the new JSONL) so prior tokens are counted in both sessions.
premortem.cause: session_id-keyed dedup assumes one engine conversation maps to at most one Anchor session and one cost source, but persist→rediscover, switch_engine, and seed/resume all create legitimate second identities for the same underlying work.
premortem.mitigation: Dedup on the ENGINE side, not the Anchor side: key ingested usage by (engine_session_uuid, message_uuid or line hash) in an append-only ledger; a session's cost = sum of ledger lines attributed to it; a discovered effort whose docs carry a session_id contributes 0 (already the effort_view rule — add a rollup test pinning it). Add an invariant test: switch_engine mid-session yields total = A-part + B-part, counted once.

premortem.mode: The B2 tile fixes pass their fixture tests but the blank-window bug persists in production: the blank open was actually a WebSocket-attach race / replay-buffer timing issue on real ConPTY, not a pure function of registry state, so the deterministic-fixture reproduction 'fixed' a different, cleaner bug and the live sign-off keeps failing intermittently.
premortem.cause: Stub-PTY fixtures cannot exhibit ConPTY replay timing; the diagnosis conflated 'reproducible symptom' with 'deterministic cause'.
premortem.mitigation: Before coding, reproduce each B2 failure against the REAL PTY backend with Playwright (the project already gates UI waves this way) and record which ones survive; classify each as state-bug (fixture-testable) vs race (needs an attach-ack/replay-complete protocol change), and plan them as separate items.

premortem.mode: Warm opens are blank anyway for the sessions users actually click: brownfield/discovered efforts and pre-v7 sessions predate summarize-on-finish, general sessions were excluded from persistent surfaces entirely (the known surface gap), and killed sessions with failed summary generation have no cache — so the majority of REAL tiles fall to the honest-degraded seed and the headline promise ('any tile narrates') reads as broken on day one.
premortem.cause: Summary/doc coverage was extrapolated from recent, healthy sessions; the historical registry is dominated by sessions created before the hooks existed.
premortem.mitigation: Ship a one-time backfill wave FIRST (batch summarize-from-persisted-docs/transcripts through the stubbed-in-tests runner seam, throttled live), measure coverage % on the real registry before/after, and make the degraded seed still substantive: doc list + lane + dates + last transcript tail, which the W3 synthesizer already knows how to build.

premortem.mode: Gemini sessions — a large fraction on this both-subscriptions host under the 5:1 policy — all show 'unmeasured', so the rollup bifurcates into 'measured Claude truth' and a growing unmeasured mass; worse, an engine-switched session shows the Claude half measured and the Gemini half missing with no marker, making the number look complete when it isn't.
premortem.cause: The plan scoped Gemini as an edge ('explicitly unmeasured') while W8 policy makes it mainline; per-session partial measurement was never modeled.
premortem.mitigation: Model measurement per ENGINE SEGMENT, not per session: each segment is measured/unmeasured independently and the session badge shows 'partial (gemini segment unmeasured)'; investigate Gemini CLI's own session/telemetry files as a fast follow rather than pretending completeness.

premortem.mode: Existing suites go red and the fix quietly rewrites history: a v4 rollup test asserts exact totals over a fixture registry (imported/discovered contribute 0 AND nothing else contributes), so adding RUN-cost ingestion changes the totals; under wave pressure the 'unmodified' constraint flips to 'tests updated to match', deleting the very assertions that pinned no-fabrication.
premortem.cause: Criterion said 'stay GREEN unmodified' without first auditing which assertions pin closed-world totals.
premortem.mitigation: Audit test_* for closed-world rollup assertions in wave 0 and decide EXPLICITLY per test: additive-compatible (new source off by default in fixtures) vs legitimately superseded (documented in the plan, not improvised); require the new states to be opt-in via the sidecar-seam env so legacy fixtures see the legacy world.

premortem.mode: The 5AM healthcheck (or the pytest suite) globs the REAL ~/.claude store: the seam defaults to the live path and one code path (backfill, drift-warn, or the healthcheck's v-next surface walk) forgets the override — the healthcheck ingests John's real overnight swarm sessions into a synthetic project's rollup, or a test 'finalizes' real sidecars, polluting real data the way the CODE_DIR-swap healthcheck bug once redirected the registry.
premortem.cause: A default-live seam is one missed env-set away from touching production state, and this codebase has hit exactly this failure class before (v9 healthcheck anchor-repo probe).
premortem.mitigation: Make the seam FAIL-CLOSED under test: paths.py detects ANCHOR_DATA_DIR/healthcheck mode and refuses (raises) to resolve the live sidecar root unless ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR is explicitly set; add a STUB-GATE test asserting the healthcheck run never opens a path under the real home store (spy on the resolver), mirroring the never-8777 guard pattern.

premortem.mode: Concurrent end paths tear the cost ledger: the user clicks Kill→Boneyard while reconcile_and_advance finalizes the same session during a drain; both write a cost record through the known non-atomic registry/effort-history write path — result is either two RUN records for one session (double count) or a truncated JSON index that the next boot reads as corrupt, taking the whole efforts view down.
premortem.cause: Finalize was specified as 'idempotent' but implemented over rnd_registry/effort_history writers that the 2026-07-08 architecture review already flagged as non-atomic and lock-incomplete; idempotence requires an atomic check-and-write, not two steps.
premortem.mitigation: Land the atomic-write hardening (temp-file+rename under WRITE_LOCK) for the specific files finalize touches BEFORE the finalize wave; make finalize a compare-and-set keyed on session_id ('cost_final' flag set atomically with the record) and add a stress test that races kill/close/reconcile 50× and asserts exactly one record and parseable indexes.

premortem.mode: The zombie-hunter and reaper fight the new warm-resume behavior: click-spawned orientation sessions whose browser tab closes have no attached PTY stream and no owning job; under load the swarm-warning banner fills with them, or the boot reaper (which now preserves STATUS_IDLE worktrees) accumulates dozens of parked orientation worktrees that never get cleaned, eating disk and making 'git worktree list' unusable.
premortem.cause: Every resume creates a real live-owner-less-looking session by design, and the preservation rule added in W6 has no complementary expiry.
premortem.mitigation: Tag click-resumed orientation sessions with an origin marker the live-owner computation treats as owned-for-N-minutes, then auto-park them (graceful close, docs persisted) rather than leaving them RUNNING; add a bounded parked-worktree budget with oldest-first graceful eviction (docs are already persisted to main, so eviction loses nothing) and surface the count on the dashboard.

premortem.mode: The before/after undercount criterion reports a meaningless number: historical sidecars were pruned (FM-03), the backfill can only attribute the surviving few via the ambiguous slug+mtime heuristic (FM-02), so the headline 'we recovered X% of previously-invisible cost' is either tiny (looks like the feature failed) or built on misattributed records (looks like it worked but lies).
premortem.cause: Criterion 7 depends transitively on assumptions 2 and 3 holding RETROACTIVELY, over data written before any capture discipline existed.
premortem.mitigation: Reframe the criterion prospectively: measure capture-rate on NEW sessions for one week post-deploy (target: ≥90% of Claude-engine sessions measured) and report historical backfill as best-effort with an explicit 'attributed / surviving / total' breakdown instead of a single recovered-% figure.

ideas.idea: Spike-first sidecar contract probe: before any pipeline code, run a REAL interactive claude PTY for 3 turns, kill it, and diff the produced ~/.claude/projects/<slug> JSONL against parser expectations; pin the observed shape as the canonical fixture and gate the whole capture design on this spike's findings (per FM-01).
ideas.note: Receipt: FM-01 says the parser may find nothing it recognizes; the spike converts an assumed sidecar schema into an observed one before a single wave is planned.

ideas.idea: Sum-over-message-usage parser design: compute session cost as the sum of per-message usage blocks (not find-the-session-total-record), with explicit states 'measured', 'partial: resumed elsewhere', and 'unmeasured' — never a guessed total.
ideas.note: Directly mitigates FM-01's relabeled zero-by-omission; partial state is honest, not fabricated.

ideas.idea: Capture engine_session_id AT LAUNCH: watch the project slug dir for the new JSONL created within a tight window while holding the session lock (or parse the PTY banner), store the UUID on the registry record; any record without a captured UUID is honestly 'uncorrelated' — never mtime-guessed after the fact.
ideas.note: Kills FM-02 (wrong-session attribution) at the root; correlation becomes a fact recorded at start, not a heuristic at end.

ideas.idea: Eager finalize + heartbeat snapshot: copy the usage summary into .anchor/ at EVERY end path (kill, close/park, drain, finish) plus a periodic heartbeat copy for long-lived sessions, so reconcile-dead weeks later reads Anchor's own durable snapshot, never the prunable ~/.claude store.
ideas.note: Mitigates FM-03; the sidecar is treated as transient source, .anchor/ as the durable record — consistent with the v8 persist-before-reap keystone philosophy.

ideas.idea: Tokens+time as first-class measured truth; dollars OPTIONAL and shown only when the engine itself reported a nonzero costUSD — render 'N tok · Xm (subscription)' on the Max-subscription host; a no-own-pricing-table rule locked at plan level so no wave adds one.
ideas.note: Mitigates FM-04's fabrication-by-multiplication; 'measured truth' means what the engine reported, nothing derived.

ideas.idea: Append-only usage LEDGER keyed by (engine_session_uuid, message_uuid/line-hash): a session's cost = sum of ledger lines attributed to it; re-ingesting the same sidecar (engine-switch relaunch, continue-session resumed history) is idempotent by key, making double-count structurally impossible.
ideas.note: FM-08's engine-side dedup; the invariant 'switch_engine total = A-part + B-part counted once' becomes a pinned test.

ideas.idea: Rollup dedup pinned by test: persist docs (source=discovered) AND attach a RUN cost record for the SAME session_id in one test, assert the rollup counts the cost exactly once and the discovered doc-effort contributes 0 — extending the existing effort_view session_id rule into the cost domain.
ideas.note: Directly implements criterion 3's proof obligation and pins the FM-08 discovered-vs-run coexistence case.

ideas.idea: Wave-0 closed-world test audit: enumerate every existing rollup/persist assertion (v4/v8 suites), classify each as additive-compatible (new cost source off-by-default in legacy fixtures via the sidecar-seam env) vs legitimately superseded (documented in the plan) — no improvised test rewrites under wave pressure.
ideas.note: FM-12 mitigation; the 'existing suites stay green unmodified' constraint is only satisfiable if the new source is opt-in for legacy fixtures, and that must be decided now.

ideas.idea: Fail-closed sidecar-root seam in paths.py: under ANCHOR_DATA_DIR/healthcheck/test mode the resolver RAISES rather than resolving the live ~/.claude store unless ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR is explicitly set; a STUB-GATE test spies the resolver and asserts the healthcheck run never opens a real-home path — mirroring the never-8777 guard.
ideas.note: FM-13; the CODE_DIR-swap healthcheck bug is the historical receipt that this exact class of leak happens here.

ideas.idea: Atomic-write hardening LANDS BEFORE the finalize wave: temp-file+rename under WRITE_LOCK for exactly the files finalize touches (registry, effort index, ledger), finalize as compare-and-set on a cost_final flag keyed by session_id, plus a 50× kill/close/reconcile race stress test asserting exactly one record and parseable indexes.
ideas.note: FM-14; the 2026-07-08 architecture review already flagged non-atomic writes in rnd_registry/effort_history as the #1 durability bug — this wave has an existing receipt.

ideas.idea: B2 tile bugs reproduced against the REAL ConPTY backend first (Playwright), each classified state-bug (fixture-testable) vs attach-race (needs a WS attach-ack/replay-complete protocol change), and planned as separate items — only then fixed, with per-tile-class screenshot sign-off.
ideas.note: FM-09; a deterministic-fixture 'fix' of a race would pass tests and fail live — the classification step is the mitigation.

ideas.idea: WS attach-ack/replay-complete handshake: the terminal window renders only after the server acks the attach and signals replay-buffer-complete, eliminating the blank-window race as a protocol property rather than a timing hope.
ideas.note: The concrete engineering shape FM-09's race classification will likely demand; pre-scoping it avoids a mid-wave surprise.

ideas.idea: Two-step tile affordance: click = PASSIVE warm view (cached summary + doc-role narration + pending NEXT-PROMPT as paste-not-submit, zero PTY, zero engine turns, free); an explicit '▶ Resume live' control = spawn + orientation. Reuse an already-live session for the same effort instead of spawning a sibling.
ideas.note: Mitigates FM-06 and FM-07 simultaneously; 'reliably opens a warm terminal that narrates' is satisfied by the two-step without dashboard browsing costing 250k tokens.

ideas.idea: Orientation runs harness-enforced read-only: if any auto-executed narration survives the design fork, it runs as a one-shot plan-mode job through job_runner (permission_mode='plan', like Gandalf shards) — NEVER a seeded turn on the live interactive PTY; ACTION prompts remain v10 paste-NOT-submit, pinned by a test asserting no ACTION prompt is ever auto-submitted.
ideas.note: FM-06: a prompt-text 'read-only classifier' is judgment with extra steps; plan-mode is the only enforcement the codebase already trusts (Gandalf Stage-A precedent).

ideas.idea: One-time summary BACKFILL wave ships FIRST: batch-summarize from persisted docs/transcripts through the runner seam (stubbed in tests, throttled live) for brownfield, pre-v7, general, and failed-summary sessions; measure coverage % on the real registry before/after so 'any tile narrates' is true on day one, not aspirational.
ideas.note: FM-10; the known general-session surface gap and pre-summarize-on-finish sessions are the tiles users actually click.

ideas.idea: Substantive degraded seed: when no cached summary exists even after backfill, the warm view still shows doc list + lane + dates + last transcript tail (the W3 synthesizer already builds this) — 'degraded' never means blank.
ideas.note: FM-10's second half; guarantees the non-blank-window criterion (4) for every tile class including discovered.

ideas.idea: Per-ENGINE-SEGMENT measurement model: each engine segment of a session is measured/unmeasured independently; the session badge shows 'partial (gemini segment unmeasured)' rather than a complete-looking Claude-only number; Gemini CLI telemetry-file investigation is an explicit fast-follow item, not silently pretended complete.
ideas.note: FM-11; on this both-subscriptions 5:1 host a per-session boolean would systematically lie about switched sessions.

ideas.idea: Live drift tripwire the healthcheck CAN run: a NON-model, read-only parse of the most recent real sidecars already on disk, report.warn (never red, per the locked severity rule) when zero of the last N real session files yield usage — catching a CLI-upgrade schema rename that pinned fixtures would mask forever.
ideas.note: FM-05; the healthcheck's all-model-calls-stubbed contract makes a stubbed tripwire useless — read-only real-file parsing is the loophole that respects the contract.

ideas.idea: Capture-rate stamped on the rollup itself: 'measured 14/17 sessions (30d)' rendered next to the totals, so capture decay is visible on the dashboard where John looks daily, not only in 5AM reports.
ideas.note: FM-05's second mitigation; also makes the honesty contract legible — the number advertises its own coverage.

ideas.idea: Prospective undercount measurement: reframe criterion (7) as capture-rate on NEW sessions for one week post-deploy (target ≥90% of Claude-engine sessions measured), with historical backfill reported as an explicit 'attributed / surviving / total' breakdown — never a single recovered-% headline built on pruned or misattributed sidecars.
ideas.note: FM-16; a retrospective-only number is uncomputable (FM-03) or a lie (FM-02) — the prospective frame is the honest observable.

ideas.idea: Orientation-session lifecycle tags for the zombie-hunter: click-resumed sessions carry an origin marker the live-owner computation treats as owned-for-N-minutes, then auto-park (graceful close, docs persisted); a bounded parked-worktree budget with oldest-first graceful eviction (docs already persisted to main → eviction loses nothing) plus a dashboard count.
ideas.note: FM-15; without this the W6 keep-idle-worktrees rule + warm resume accumulates unbounded parked worktrees and floods the swarm banner with false orphans — a safety-critical surface per the 2026-06-30 swarm-warning fix.

ideas.idea: Healthcheck gains a fully-stubbed capture+finalize walk: a fake sidecar fixture (pinned from the B1 spike) is written into the temp ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR, a stub session is started/killed, and the check asserts a RUN cost record with the fixture's exact totals lands in the temp registry — extending the v2–v5 surface-walk pattern.
ideas.note: Criterion 6 names this explicitly; the existing check_rnd_vN_surface pattern is the template, so cost is low.

ideas.idea: One live smoke run as deploy sign-off: after deploy, run one real interactive session, kill it, and assert the rollup delta equals the sidecar's reported usage (tokens exact, time within tolerance) — the only place a REAL sidecar meets the parser outside the drift tripwire.
ideas.note: Criterion 1 requires it verbatim; also the project's established live-sign-off discipline (the v4 lesson).

ideas.idea: 'Unmeasured' as a first-class visual state in the rollup UI: a distinct badge/color for unmeasured vs $0.00/0-tok, with hover text naming the reason (sidecar pruned, uncorrelated, gemini segment, pre-feature session) — the reason enum comes from the finalize pipeline, not free text.
ideas.note: Criterion 2 requires the distinction; an enum of reasons makes it machine-verifiable and testable rather than cosmetic.

ideas.idea: NEXT-PROMPT.md and the cached summary become the warm view's narration spine: the passive view renders 'what was done' (cached summary), 'what was produced' (doc-roles map with /report//artifact links), and 'what comes next' (the durable NEXT-PROMPT.md / pending_paste) — all three already exist as durable artifacts, so narration is a render, not a model call.
ideas.note: The North Star's narrate/produce/next triplet maps 1:1 onto v10/v8 artifacts already on disk; zero new model spend for the common case.

ideas.idea: Cost ledger heartbeat piggybacks the existing 120s session-autosave heartbeat (2026-07-07) rather than adding a second timer — one periodic hook does transcript persist + usage snapshot.
ideas.note: Oranges foresight: two independent heartbeats on the same session invite drift and double writes; the autosave hook already fires at every point B4 needs.

ideas.idea: One-shot job_runner jobs join the same ledger: the durable job path (lane launches, Gandalf shards, summarizer runs) already parses stream-json usage — route its totals through the SAME append-only ledger keyed by engine session UUID so 'every Anchor session — interactive ConPTY or one-shot job' is literally one code path.
ideas.note: The North Star's 'or one-shot job' clause; unifying prevents the interactive and job pipelines from disagreeing on dedup keys later.

ideas.idea: Registry-state fixture capture tooling: a small dev command that snapshots a project's live session_registry + effort store into an anonymized fixture directory, so the B2 Playwright reproductions run against CAPTURED real states (criterion 4's 'captured registry-state fixtures') instead of hand-built ones.
ideas.note: The criterion names captured fixtures; hand-authored states are how the fixture-passes-production-fails trap (FM-09) starts.

ideas.idea: Lock the fork decision in the North Star doc as a written amendment: orientation = auto-executed READ-ONLY narration via plan-mode one-shot (or fully passive render if the spike shows plan-mode unenforceable on the chosen path); ACTION = paste-not-submit, always — recorded before Stage 2 so no wave relitigates it.
ideas.note: Criterion 5 says 'the fork is resolved, locked in the North Star doc'; leaving it implicit is how FM-06 ships.

ideas.idea: Gemini CLI usage-capture spike (fast-follow scoped, not this plan's gate): inventory what session/telemetry files the gemini CLI and agy dispatcher leave on disk, and whether a UUID-at-launch correlation is possible — outcome feeds the per-segment model but does NOT block the Claude-path waves.
ideas.note: FM-11's investigate-don't-pretend clause; explicitly sequenced as non-blocking so the 5:1 host reality doesn't stall the whole plan.

ideas.idea: Boneyard entries carry the final cost block: when a session is killed-to-Boneyard, its finalized usage rides on the boneyard entry, so discarded work's spend remains visible history rather than vanishing with the tile.
ideas.note: Every end path finalizes (criterion 1) — Boneyard-kill is an end path; surfacing it there is a one-field render on data the finalize already produced.

ideas.idea: Weekly cost digest email/notification summarizing per-project measured spend and capture rate.
ideas.note: Reporting cadence/notification is a new surface; no criterion asks for push reporting — the rollup + dashboard stamp cover the honesty goal.

ideas.idea: Per-session cost BUDGETS with a warn/park threshold (auto-park a session that crosses N tokens).
ideas.note: Enforcement/limits is a different feature; the North Star is measurement honesty, not spend control. Park in Grasscatcher — it becomes cheap once the ledger exists.

ideas.idea: Cross-project cost analytics view (trend charts, per-lane spend over time, engine mix).
ideas.note: Analytics beyond the existing rollup window (lifetime/30d) traces to no criterion; the ledger makes it a later render-only feature.

ideas.idea: Export the usage ledger as CSV for external accounting.
ideas.note: No criterion mentions export; trivially buildable later off the append-only ledger.

ideas.idea: Retention policy for .anchor/ usage snapshots (compaction of old ledger lines into per-session totals after M months).
ideas.note: Premature: snapshot volume is tiny JSON; add compaction only if the store measurably grows. Grasscatcher with the receipt that FM-03 argues for MORE retention, not less, right now.
